Draft handover, 26 September 2026. No files were written. File reads failed with a sandbox error; this follows the supplied skill text, but the Conductor, templates and mechanical audit remain unchecked. All proposed choices need review.

**Questions for the next planning session**

These are recorded questions, not requests for an immediate reply:

- Must “iOS” mean an App Store app? Assumption: an iPhone browser pilot is acceptable; native delivery remains unresolved.
- How many people, and who may edit? Assumption: one household, up to eight invited adults, equal recipe access.
- Must shopping work without reception? Assumption: online use first; offline writes deferred.
- What spending and hosting region are acceptable? Assumption: target $0 recurring; no paid services or region selection authorized.
- Is saving and sharing text recipes the best first slice? Assumption: yes.
- What export, retention and deletion behavior do you expect? Assumption: preserve data, provide recovery, defer destructive features.
- Does the audit readback below expose any unacceptable omissions? No acceptance assumed.

**`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`**

State: draft interview; owner: project creator; next checkpoint: resolve assumptions and approve one slice.

Purpose: a private family recipe collection, eventually including photos and a shared grocery list. Success for the pilot: two family members can save and retrieve the same recipe across devices without developer assistance.

Proposed architecture: one responsive web application using React and TypeScript, with a managed authentication/database service. Supabase is a candidate, subject to current cost, limits and region checks. Avoid a custom Python server initially.

Modules: identity/household membership, recipes, later photos and groceries. Keep provider calls behind small data-access modules; no generic plugin framework.

Flow: authenticated browser → data-access module → database authorization checks → household records. The server enforces membership; filtering the interface is insufficient.

Use household identifiers now because sharing requires ownership boundaries. Future photo objects inherit those boundaries. Grocery items remain separate from recipe ingredients because families also buy unrelated items.

Build boundary: text recipe creation and retrieval with authenticated household sharing. Photos, groceries, native iOS delivery and premium remain future slices. No payment integration or speculative subscription framework.

**`docs/ENGINEERING.md`**

State: draft; assumptions above apply.

| ID | Requirement | Delivery |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | Access on desktop web and iPhone | Browser pilot; native unresolved |
| R2 | Persist and share family recipes | Slice 001 |
| R3 | Recipe photos | Later slice |
| R4 | Shared grocery list | Later slice |
| R5 | Household privacy and authentication | Slice 001 |
| R6 | Premium for other families | Deferred |
| R7 | Recover recipe data and contain costs | Slice 001 |

Initial model: household; membership linking authenticated user to household; recipe with UUID, household ID, creator ID, title, ingredient text, method text and creation timestamp. Ingredients remain text; automatic quantity conversion is deferred.

Accounts and membership are provisioned manually for the pilot. Clients cannot grant themselves membership. Deny anonymous and foreign-household access at the database boundary. Keep privileged credentials out of browser bundles. Render recipe content as text; validate required fields and length limits on the server.

Initial synchronization means retrieval after refresh or returning to the app. Display loading, empty, saved and failed states. Preserve entered text on failure; never announce success before persistence. Reuse a submission UUID when retrying to avoid duplicates.

Use version control, reviewed migrations, pinned dependencies and a documented setup. Log operation failures without recipe contents or credentials. Document export and restoration, and verify a round trip using disposable data.

Definition of done: slice evidence passes, setup works from a clean checkout, assumptions are updated, and no unauthorized scope appears.

**`docs/DECISION-LOG.md`**

All entries are proposed or deferred, not accepted.

| Decision | Status | Options, recommendation and revisit trigger |
|---|---|---|
| D1 Delivery | Proposed | Browser pilot versus native plus web. Start browser-first for weekend capacity; revisit if installation or native capabilities are essential. |
| D2 Backend | Proposed | Managed service versus custom server. Prefer managed; revisit after pricing, region and recovery checks. |
| D3 Sync | Proposed | Refresh-based versus realtime/offline. Start refresh-based; revisit during grocery-list planning. |
| D4 Ownership | Proposed | Household membership versus shared login. Use individual accounts and household ownership; revisit roles when invitations are added. |
| D5 Premium | Deferred | Subscription provider and entitlements await demonstrated demand. |
| D6 Irreversible choices | Deferred | Region, payments, public API contracts and deletion require explicit human confirmation before implementation. |

**`docs/SLICE-001-shared-text-recipes.md`**

State: proposed; estimated target: two weekends, reassessed after setup.

Outcome: two preprovisioned household members can create, list and read text recipes on iPhone and desktop.

Includes R1’s browser pilot, R2, R5 and R7. Excludes editing, deletion, photos, groceries, offline writes, realtime subscriptions, native packaging and billing.

Acceptance evidence:

1. Save on iPhone; retrieve identical content on desktop after refresh.
2. Sign out and back in; recipes persist.
3. Anonymous and foreign-household reads and writes fail, including direct requests.
4. Failed submission retains text; retry produces one recipe.
5. Export and restore disposable recipes successfully.
6. Record automated authorization/retry results and a short real-device walkthrough.

Before provisioning, resolve provider limits and region. Stop and replan if the time or spending boundary cannot hold.

**Audit readback**

Scope is bounded, but assumptions, native delivery and infrastructure approval remain open. Automated audit and local review recording remain pending.

**`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`**

State: interview incomplete. Owner: project creator.

Purpose: a private family recipe collection with shared groceries. Success means family members can reliably retrieve saved recipes across devices.

Proposed architecture: one responsive TypeScript/React application, one managed authentication/database service, and private photo storage when needed. Provider and hosting selection remain pending cost and region checks. No separate Python service initially.

Modules and responsibilities:

- Identity and household membership: establish who can access each household.
- Recipes: validate, save, list, and display recipe content.
- Photos, later: authorize uploads and retrieval.
- Groceries, later: maintain a household list with independently editable items.

Data flow: authenticated browser → recipe service → database authorization → household-scoped records. Clients never receive administrative credentials.

Internal interfaces: create recipe, list household recipes, retrieve recipe. Keep provider access behind a small module; public APIs are deferred.

Synchronization initially means server persistence plus refresh when opening or returning to the app and a manual refresh control. Live collaboration and offline writes are separate decisions.

Extension points: household identifiers support future isolation; photo and grocery modules attach through recipe/household identifiers. No billing framework or speculative plugin system.

**`docs/ENGINEERING.md`**

| R4 | Recipe photos | Later slice |

Initial model: Household; Membership(user ID, household ID); Recipe(UUID, household ID, title, ingredients text, instructions text, creator, server timestamp). Memberships are manually provisioned initially. No shared passwords.

Authorization must enforce membership in the backend on every read/write. Users cannot grant themselves membership. Validate required fields and lengths server-side; render recipe text safely. Keep secrets outside source control; logs exclude recipe contents, credentials, and session tokens.

Failed saves retain entered text and show failure. Reuse a submission UUID on retry to prevent duplicate recipes. Offline submission shows an explicit error. Future editing must define conflict handling before implementation.

Standards: small modules, typed boundaries, committed dependency lockfile, documented environment setup, versioned migrations, and no unrelated refactoring.

**Planning handoff: provisional, awaiting owner review.** These are proposed contents for four files under `docs/`; nothing was saved. Local file reads failed, so the supplied skill text informed this draft, but its Conductor and templates remain unread. Mechanical audit was not run. All technical choices below are assumptions, not accepted decisions.

**Questions for later review**

1. Does “iOS” require an App Store app, or would an iPhone website installed on the home screen suffice?
2. Must the grocery list work without internet?
3. Who may join, invite others, edit recipes, or remove content? Will children have accounts?
4. What monthly spending ceiling and hosting region are acceptable?
5. Is creating a recipe on one device and reading it on another the right first milestone?
6. Are the assumptions, privacy controls, deferred features, and incomplete audit acceptable for further planning?

Working assumptions: one family, individual accounts, equal editing rights, online use, home-screen web app initially, no paid services without approval. Native distribution, offline shopping, residency, and deletion policy remain unresolved.

**`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — State: draft interview**

Purpose: privately collect family recipes and coordinate shopping across phones and computers. Constraints: weekend development, near-zero budget, modest Python/JavaScript experience.

Proposed structure:

- One responsive web application, provisionally React and TypeScript.
- Managed authentication, PostgreSQL, and private photo storage, provisionally Supabase. Provider suitability, current costs, and limits require verification before commitment.
- Modules: identity/family access, recipes, photos, groceries. Keep these in one repository and deployment.
- Data flow: signed-in browser → authenticated data operations → database membership checks → family records. Photo access follows the same membership boundary.
- Internal recipe operations: create, list, read; later edit. Keep provider calls in a small data module. No public API commitment.

The database is authoritative. Initially, saving waits for server confirmation; other devices fetch changes on refresh. Automatic updates and offline writes are deferred.

Future connections: photos reference recipes; grocery items belong to a family and may reference a recipe. Premium is a later product decision, with no billing code or subscription schema now.

Current build boundary: authenticated recipe creation and retrieval across devices. Other modules are planned only.

**`docs/ENGINEERING.md` — State: draft interview**

Requirements ledger:

| ID | Requirement | Boundary |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | iPhone and desktop access | Slice 001; native iOS unresolved |
| R2 | Private family access | Slice 001 |
| R3 | Create, list, read synced recipes | Slice 001 |
| R4 | Recipe photos | Later slice |
| R5 | Shared grocery list | Later slice |
| R6 | Honest save/error states | Slice 001 |
| R7 | Focused verification | Slice 001 |
| R8 | Export and recovery | Before irreplaceable family data |
| R9 | Premium for other families | Deferred investigation |

Initial model: Family; Membership linking authenticated user to family; Recipe with UUID, family ID, title, ingredient text, method text, author, and timestamps. Require title, ingredients, and method. Later models: Photo and GroceryItem, each scoped to family.

Database rules enforce membership on every read and write. Users cannot grant themselves membership. Administrative credentials never enter browser code. Logs exclude recipe contents, photos, passwords, and tokens.

Use client-generated recipe IDs so retrying an uncertain save cannot duplicate a recipe. Failed saves retain the form and explain retry. Do not claim offline persistence.

Use versioned migrations, pinned dependencies, documented environment variables, and small module boundaries. No destructive migrations or deletion features in this slice.

Definition of done: R1–R3 and R6–R7 pass; setup is reproducible; no secrets committed; limitations documented. Use synthetic recipes until residency and recovery are settled.

**`docs/DECISION-LOG.md` — State: draft interview**

| ID | Status | Choice, alternatives, revisit trigger |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Proposed | Home-screen web app over separate native/web clients; revisit if App Store distribution or device capabilities are essential. |
| D2 | Proposed | Managed backend over custom Python server; revisit after checking costs, account requirements, export, and operations burden. |
| D3 | Proposed | Online saves and refresh over offline synchronization; revisit if grocery-store connectivity makes this unusable. |
| D4 | Proposed | Separate accounts with manually provisioned family membership over shared credentials; revisit before inviting another family. |
| D5 | Deferred | Premium and payment provider; reopen only after family usage demonstrates value and someone commits to paying. |
| D6 | Needs confirmation | Hosting region, deletion policy, and public API contracts; no irreversible commitment without explicit owner confirmation. |

**`docs/SLICE-001-shared-recipes.md` — State: proposed, not approved**

Outcome: two pre-provisioned family members can share a text recipe between iPhone and desktop.

Includes sign-in/out, membership enforcement, recipe form, list/detail views, responsive layout, loading/error states, and focused tests.

Excludes editing, deletion, photos, grocery lists, invitations, offline mode, native packaging, billing, and generic verification infrastructure.

Acceptance evidence:

- Member A creates a recipe; member B retrieves identical content after refresh.
- Refresh preserves a confirmed save; retry creates no duplicate.
- Signed-out and different-family users cannot read or create family recipes, including direct requests.
- A failed save preserves entered text and shows no success message.
- Record automated results and a manual iPhone/desktop walkthrough.

Budget: one weekend checkpoint. If incomplete, revise the brief before expanding scope.
